description: Theta* finds short *any-angle* paths on a grid: paths of straight segments between cell centres, not only along grid edges. It runs A* over the 8-connected moves with the Euclidean distance as heuristic. When it reaches a cell `s′` from `s`, it tests whether `s′` can see the parent of `s`. If it can, `s′` takes that parent as its own, so the path skips `s` in one straight line. The path is not always the shortest any-angle path, but it is never longer than the cheapest 8-connected path. Use it for natural-looking paths for robots and game characters.

papers.authors: Alex Nash, Kenny Daniel, Sven Koenig, Ariel Felner
papers.title: Theta*: Any-Angle Path Planning on Grids
papers.venue: Proceedings of the Twenty-Second AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence

lineage.source: heuristic-search, src/grid/theta.rs: "Both are A* over the 8-connected moves of a LineOfSight grid that lets a path leave the grid edges"
